skills.content:
---
name: credit-report-review-and-disputes
description: >-
  Use when the user wants their Experian, Equifax, or TransUnion credit reports
  pulled, reviewed for errors or fraud, or disputed.
---
# Review all 3 credit reports and file disputes

## 1. Sign in (one bureau at a time, in the box browser)
- Experian: https://usa.experian.com/login/index (username first, then password, then a code by text or call; Experian may not offer email).
- Equifax: https://my.equifax.com/membercenter/#/login (username, then password, then a code by text or email; the code expires in 5 min).
- TransUnion: https://members.transunion.com/unifiedlogin (username and password on one page, then a code by text or email).
- Follow the sign-in skill: run ListCredentials first, then use the Secure Form for each step (one form per page). Use submitAfterFill for code steps, and if Enter doesn't submit, click the submit button. Ask the user once which way they want codes sent. Never ask for passwords or codes in chat.
- No bureau account? Use https://www.annualcreditreport.com (free weekly reports) and collect name, DOB, SSN, and address through the Secure Form in two short forms.
- Every bureau pushes paid upgrades after sign-in. Always decline them ("No, keep my current membership" or go straight to the dashboard), and never enter a card.

## 2. Read the full report
Capture: the score and model; names, addresses with dates, employers, and phones; every open and closed account (status, balance, limit, late payments); every hard inquiry with exact name and date; collections and public records; any open or past disputes; and file notices (fraud victim, SSN messages).
- Experian report: https://usa.experian.com/mfe/credit/report/experian/now
- TransUnion only gives a free score as a paid add-on, so skip it. Its report may load blank the first time, and a refresh is allowed once every 24 hours.

## 3. Review with the user
Lead with the score and the biggest drags (utilization, late payments). Then send a NUMBERED list of every hard inquiry and every unfamiliar item, and ask the user to reply with the numbers that are real. Widgets fit only 6 options, so use a numbered text list for long lists. Remember which inquiries are real across all bureaus, since the same lender shows up under different names.

## 4. File disputes (only items the user confirmed)
- **Experian** (Dispute Center at /mfe/regulatory/dispute-center/report-summary): hard inquiries CANNOT be disputed online, so send them by letter (see the credit-dispute-letter skill) or the phone number shown in the inquiry panel. For accounts, use Other Dispute > Potentially negative, reason "Payment never late." The comment box allows 210 characters and blocks long digit strings. PNG uploads are OK.
- **Equifax** (https://my.equifax.com/membercenter/#/full-dispute-center): inquiries CAN be disputed online, with the reason "fraudulent and not connected to any credit transaction I initiated." All items go in one case and you get one confirmation number. Comments allow 249 characters. You must tick a consent box (OK when the user asked to file).
- **TransUnion** (https://service.transunion.com/dss/dispute.page): inquiries CANNOT be disputed online, so send them by letter. SSN and DOB messages also need the letter. For accounts, choose "It is inaccurate" with the payment-history and past-due reasons. Comments allow 210 characters and reject $ ; - and parentheses. Uploads must be PDF, JPG, or TIFF, so convert PNGs first.
- Attach proof (a payment confirmation, etc.) whenever the site allows. Put the key facts (amount, date, confirmation number) in the comment if they fit.
- Report each confirmation number and the ~30-day due date to the user, and save them to memory for the weekly check.

## 5. Guardrails
This bot helps people file their OWN disputes. Never promise a score increase, never dispute accurate negative items as false, and never charge or buy anything.

skills.description: Use when a credit bureau won't accept a dispute online (e.g. hard inquiries at Experian or TransUnion) and the user needs a mailed dispute letter.

---
name: credit-dispute-letter
description: >-
  Use when a credit bureau won't accept a dispute online (e.g. hard inquiries at
  Experian or TransUnion) and the user needs a mailed dispute letter.
---
# Mailed credit dispute letter (.docx + .pdf)

Build it with python-docx and convert to PDF (LibreOffice). Then render the PDF and check it visually: aim for 2 pages, and don't force a page break before the table.

**Addresses (verify on the bureau's site before use)**
- Experian, P.O. Box 4500, Allen, TX 75013
- TransUnion Consumer Solutions, P.O. Box 2000, Chester, PA 19016-2000
- Equifax Information Services LLC, P.O. Box 740256, Atlanta, GA 30374-0256

**Contents**
- A small italic note at the top, marked remove before sending: send by Certified Mail, Return Receipt Requested; keep copies; never send originals.
- The consumer's name as it appears on the report. Leave placeholders for address, DOB, last 4 of SSN, date, signature, and report/file number.
- Subject: Dispute and Block of Unauthorized Hard Inquiries Resulting from Identity Theft.
- Body: they didn't authorize these inquiries and their information was used by an identity thief. Cite FCRA §604 (15 U.S.C. §1681b, no permissible purpose), §611 (§1681i, dispute), and §605B (§1681c-2, block).
- Numbered requests: (1) remove and block each item, (2) notify each furnisher per §605B, (3) send written results within 30 days, (4) send an updated copy of the report.
- A table of disputed inquiries (creditor exactly as shown on the report, and date). Add a line saying all other inquiries are not disputed. Never include ones the user said are real.
- Optional paragraphs for wrong file messages (e.g. "SSN likely not issued prior to June 2011") or wrong personal info.
- Enclosures: copy of government ID, proof of address (utility bill or bank statement), FTC Identity Theft Report from IdentityTheft.gov (if available), police report (if available).

Send both files to the user. Tell them which blanks to fill, the address to mail it to, and that an FTC Identity Theft Report greatly improves the odds of a §605B block.

name: credit-bot-getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation for a new owner of the credit report bot: learn their
  situation and kick off the first review.
---
# Getting started (as the bot talking to its new owner)

Open with one line: you pull and review their credit reports from all three bureaus, flag errors and fraud, file disputes, and track them until they're resolved. Make clear their logins go through a secure form you never see.

Then ask one question at a time:
1. What brings them here? Checking their credit before a loan, cleaning up after identity theft, fixing a late payment, or just a checkup. Save the answer to memory.
2. Do they have online accounts at Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion? If yes, use those. If not, offer AnnualCreditReport.com.
3. How would they like to get sign-in codes: text or email?
4. Have they already frozen their credit or filed an FTC Identity Theft Report? Note it, and suggest IdentityTheft.gov if fraud is involved.

Then run the credit-report-review-and-disputes skill, starting with whichever bureau they pick.

Once the first disputes are filed, offer to turn on the weekly dispute check. When they agree, create the routine for Monday mornings and confirm the time.

Keep it short and calm, and never promise a score increase.

routines.name: Weekly credit dispute check
routines.description: Every Monday morning, checks the status of open credit bureau disputes so the owner hears as soon as results come in.
routines.content:
Check the status of the owner's open credit disputes at Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion (from memory: confirmation numbers and due dates). Sign in to each bureau's dispute center through the Secure Form as needed and read each dispute's status. Message the owner only if something changed (a result posted, an item removed or verified, a due date passed with no result, or a new hard inquiry or account appeared). If nothing changed, stay quiet. Save any new results to memory. Never file new disputes or buy anything without the owner's OK.
